system.summary: Two-part code of 367 groups: letters with 2-5 homophones mostly below 100, CV syllables, words and nulls scattered above.
system.sibling_key: Bazeries' Grand Chiffre de 1691 (587 groups) gave the design; the d'Herleville letter in the same petit chiffre with its translation gave the values. Both used.
system.notes: i/j and u/v merged; numbers and place names spelled. Key recovered for 167 of 179 groups used.

prior_solution.where: Bazeries' unpublished decipherment (1893), presumably in his papers at SHD Vincennes; not found

conditions.human_role: Supplied the Gallica PDF of Burgaud and Bazeries, Le Masque de fer (1893).

solution.what: Collated Tomokiyo's transcription with the 1819 page images: three corrections.
418 groups, 160 distinct, max 366; 46 % below 100; no Croissy step-10 structure: two-part code with letters low.
Matched control of the inferred design: the solver's wrong keys outscore the true key; 4-12 % recovery; 60 % of key given completes only 63 %.
Annealing with Veillane cribs and word-segmentation objective on the real letter: crib-farmed word salad.
Read Bazeries' Le Masque de fer (1893): he deciphered the letter with a 367-group petit chiffre; neither text nor table printed.
Transcribed Bazeries' Grand Chiffre table and verified it on four 1690-91 despatches: gives the design.
MDZ OCR of the 1819 Mémoires searched for number runs: found Louvois to d'Herleville (6 Sept 1690) in the same code with its translation.
Exact known-plaintext alignment and annealers against the translation.
Hand anchoring of the d'Herleville second paragraph and propagation between the two letters.
Both letters read: 586 of 601 tokens, 167 of 179 groups.
d'Herleville reading matches its printed translation; Feuquières text matches Catinat's Veillane memoir of 19 Jan.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 586 tokens, 167 types, fr-grand-siecle order 4: reading -2.078 per letter; random keys -3.514 (z 11.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.271 (mean -2.295, z 12.8); annealer on the real text -2.27. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions ciphertext.txt and herleville.txt; decryptions and the English translation copied from NOTES.md to texts/, beside the group alignment reading.txt; key key_petit_chiffre_1690.tsv

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): reading bodies cut out of the decryption files into texts/feuquieres1691_reading.md and texts/herleville1690_reading.md. Feuquières letter 0.545 plain and explicit (6/11 sentences; twelve unread singleton groups): demoted to decoded, not read, gap no-key-material; fraction_read 0.975 -> 0.304 (d'Herleville 183 of 601 tokens), class read -> read in part. d'Herleville letter (control) 0.667 plain, 0.833 explicit, with its printed contemporary translation: keeps read.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Verification of 14 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout, Claude Opus 5.5): gaps re-read on the page images (no slip found); 241 vous? -> me (three contexts), 54 po and 257 so (disposois, probable), 194 null, 333 et, 353 par; 145 go kept (dragons), the 'disposois [à]' slot shown as supplied. texts.label: Feuquières to Catinat, Pignerol, 25 Jan 1691
texts.summary: Feuquières acknowledges Catinat's letter of the 24th and sets out the plan for the surprise of Veillane (Avigliana): the enemy will not defend it seriously, he cannot see how to get the eighty horse to Sant'Ambrogio, and he will attack at two points and keep the dragoons from escaping. It matches Catinat's 'Mémoire pour l'entreprise de Veillane' of 19 Jan; printed in cipher in the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat, t. II pp. 283-284.
texts.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1691 French; the fr word list knows the period spelling, so the plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored texts/feuquieres1691_decryption.md with its header and commentary (plain 0.469, explicit 0.75). The reading alone, texts/feuquieres1691_reading.md: plain 0.545 (6/11), explicit 0.545 (6/11), hole rate 0.123. The five failing sentences carry three to six unread groups each (9, 19, 54, 122, 132, 257, 271, 292, 333, 353, singletons or doubletons of the petit chiffre with no value in either printed letter) plus supplied words ([par], [À]). The story is clear (Veillane, the 80 horse for Saint-Ambroise, the two roads, the dragoons), but under the bar on both measures: decoded, not read. Not workable here: no further text in this code is known; the original is at the SHD (A1 1079). 14 Nov 2026 verification: 241 = me, 54 po, 257 so, 194 null, 333 et, 353 par; read_share 0.926 (v10 rule; 0.875 before), under the 95% bar: read in part.

texts.label: Louvois to d'Herleville, Versailles, 6 Sept 1690 (control)
texts.summary: Louvois tells d'Herleville, governor of Pignerol, that the King permits him to demand the contribution of the country of Mondovì and, if he sees fit, to exempt it and let the inhabitants raze the citadel, and awaits news of his enterprise on Villefranche. Printed in cipher with its contemporary 'traduction' in the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat, t. I pp. 140-142; the alignment of the two gave the key.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1690 French: plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored the decryption file with header and commentary (plain 0.25, explicit 0.833). The reading alone, texts/herleville1690_reading.md: plain 0.667 (4/6), explicit 0.833 (5/6); the failing sentences carry the name Mondevis, 'razer' and the bracketed letters the cipher lacks (convien[s]t, servi[ce s]). The contemporary printed traduction (1819 Mémoires de Catinat t. I pp. 140-142) confirms the sense sentence by sentence. Keeps read.
